ground_truth.reason: This PR includes the feature with the fix already applied, so the vulnerability is not present

fix_commit_message:
avcodec/mmvideo: fix palette index

Fixes: 391935573/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_MMVIDEO_fuzzer-4655048979709952
Fixes: out of array access

Reviewed-by: Peter Ross <pross@xvid.org>
Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 43926e026dd8 on top of intro 63ea1660fa06 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (BufferOverflow): In FFmpeg's American Laser Games MM video decoder (libavcodec/mmvideo.c), the mm_decode_pal() function reads a 16-bit 'start' offset and a 16-bit 'count' value directly from the input bitstream and uses them, unvalidated, as the base index and loop bound for writing entries into the fixed-size s->palette[AVPALETTE_COUNT] (256-entry) array. Because neither value is bounds-checked against the array size, a maliciously crafted MM video file can cause the decoder to write palette entries far outside the bounds of the palette array, resulting in an out-of-bounds write detected by OSS-Fuzz (clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_MMVIDEO_fuzzer-4655048979709952). Root cause: The refactor in commit 63ea1660fa ("avcodec/mm: decode partial palette") replaced a previous fixed 128-iteration loop with a stream-controlled 'start' offset and 'count' loop bound, but failed to mask/clamp the resulting array index (start+i) to the valid range of the palette array, allowing attacker-controlled values to index arbitrarily far outside the array.
